desc:
You want to turn the lowercase string s into the string t of the same length. In one move you pick a position and change its letter to the next letter of the alphabet (z wraps to a) or to the previous one (a wraps to z). Letters are numbered 0..25.

  • Moving letter c to the next letter costs forward[c].
  • Moving letter c to the previous letter costs backward[c].

Positions are independent and any number of moves may be used on each. Return the minimum total cost to make s equal to t.

s = "ab", t = "ba", forward = [1, 1, ..., 1], backward = [3, 3, ..., 3]
result = 4

Turning a into b costs 1 (one forward move) and turning b into a costs 3 (one backward move).
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Each position can be handled on its own. How many different ways are there to get from one letter to another on a cycle of 26 letters?
Only two routes matter: go forward all the way around to the target, or go backward all the way. Going back and forth or around twice never helps, because costs are not negative.
Precompute a 26 × 26 table of the cheaper route for each (from, to) pair using sums of consecutive costs, then add up the table entries for all positions.
editorial: On a cycle, the only simple paths between two letters are the forward arc and the backward arc. A longer walk repeats edges and cannot be cheaper because every cost is non-negative. For letters a to b, the forward cost is forward[a] + forward[a+1] + ... up to the letter before b, and the backward cost is backward[a] + backward[a-1] + ... down to the letter after b.

Build a table cost[a][b] = min(forward arc, backward arc) in O(26²) by extending a running sum around the cycle. Then count how many positions need each (from, to) pair and sum count * cost, or simply add cost[s[i]][t[i]] for each position. Total O(n + 26²). The answer is at most 20,000 × 10,400, which fits in 32 bits.
solution:
from collections import Counter

def minShiftCost(s, t, forward, backward):
    fwd = [[0] * 26 for _ in range(26)]
    bwd = [[0] * 26 for _ in range(26)]
    for a in range(26):
        run = 0
        for d in range(26):
            fwd[a][(a + d) % 26] = run
            run += forward[(a + d) % 26]
        run = 0
        for d in range(26):
            bwd[a][(a - d) % 26] = run
            run += backward[(a - d) % 26]
    total = 0
    for (x, y), c in Counter(zip(s, t)).items():
        a, b = ord(x) - 97, ord(y) - 97
        total += c * min(fwd[a][b], bwd[a][b])
    return total
